messages:
anya: quick note — found a nasty dev onboarding footgun: someone pasted the ephemeral onboarding token into their local .env as REDWOOD_API_KEY and then wonder why background workers start failing after ~5m. reproducible.

kevin: ouch. ephemeral tokens were meant for browser sessions only. the shape is different (starts with et_). can we detect that in SDKs?

rachel: yep i saw logs: worker -> 401 when token expired, but app kept running because we only surfaced a debug log. causes confused devs.

anya: proposal: (A) SDKs validate token format and, if looks like ephemeral (et_), emit a loud warning saying "ephemeral tokens are single-session only" and point to docs; (B) sampleapp readme clearly call out not to store ephemeral tokens in REDWOOD_API_KEY.

kevin: SDK parity task: JS + Python + Go should all implement same heuristic. also add a distinct env var REDWOOD_EPHEMERAL_TOKEN for local test flows so onboarding demo can show the right pattern without encouraging persistence.

patrick: @kevin careful with adding new env var names — increases surface area for confusion. maybe instead provide a CLI helper command `rw login --ephemeral` that writes a temp token to a .session file and SDKs know to prefer .session over .env.

rachel: i like the CLI idea. less env pollution. but still we need clear error messaging when a short-lived token is used in a long-lived process. right now it just 401s.

kevin: implementation plan: 1) SDKs add token-shape detection and throw a descriptive error when used in long-lived contexts (or at least a warning with stack). 2) sampleapp: add startup check verifying token lifetime when REDWOOD_ENV_STRICT=true. 3) onboarding: change the console copy to warn about session vs service keys.

anya: can we also make runtime credential refresh non-fatal? e.g., on refresh fail, keep serving cached read-only endpoints and surface a banner. avoids total outage for devs.

patrick: yes runtime should fall back gracefully. i'll file a runtime-ux ticket to add a refresh handler that emits events to the app.

ci-bot: CI checklist: add eslint rule to sampleapp repo that flags REDWOOD_API_KEY containing prefix et_ in committed .env.example or test fixtures.

kevin: good call. i'll add a small linter rule and a unit test for token-shape detection in the JS SDK. rachel can you do a quick PR for sampleapp readme updates?

rachel: on it. i'll add a blurb and a small troubleshooting section called "Why am I getting 401s after 5 minutes?" with suggested fixes.

anya: last note: we should document precedence order for auth resolution (env var > session file > metadata > file) across SDKs. discrepancy caused a weird case where nextjs edge function used env but background worker used metadata and they picked different credentials. parity will avoid that.

kevin: agreed. will open an SDK-parity issue and tag @sdk-team. adding unit tests for env combos is high priority.

patrick: thanks, team. small mitigation first: rachel PR + ci-lint + SDK warning will remove most of the pain. follow-up: CLI session helpers + runtime graceful fallback. :rocket:
